rootNote: Teaching root chosen from WLC counts (OSHB 3d15126): H4672 מָצָא is the most frequent III-Aleph root with no second weakness (453 verb tokens: Qal 306, Niphal 139, Hiphil 8) and an active (non-stative) Qal. It is the paradigm root of GKC §74 / Paradigm O and Davidson §38. מָלֵא (249, 5 stems) and טָמֵא (162, 5 stems) have more stems but stative Qal perfects (מָלֵאתִי), which the ruling keeps as a note only. מצא has no Piel, Pual, Hitpael or Hophal in the Bible; those squares take examples from other III-Aleph roots.
source: Forms from GKC §74 + Paradigm O (Weak Verbs ל״א, PDF pp. 483-484) and Davidson, Introductory Hebrew Grammar §38 paradigm (pp. 176-177), both in /workspace/hebrew-books/ and read from page images. Squares those tables do not print follow GKC §74 applied to the strong-verb.json pattern; formBasis says which ('book' = printed in GKC or Davidson, including GKC's bracketed forms; 'rule' = regular pattern). Quiescent א is written exactly as WLC writes it. Not copied from any copyrighted chart.
verificationMethod: Each form was matched (consonants + vowel points, accents ignored, dagesh lene and plene/defective ḥolem, shureq and ḥireq-yod spellings normalized) against OSHB morphhb-wlc tokens with the same OSHB morph slot. Radicals are positional (R1 = מ, R2 = צ, R3 = א); a begadkefat radical's dagesh in dagesh-lene position is optional; Hitpael is matched both with and without sibilant metathesis (הִשְׁתַּ- / הִתְ-). The example's root (with shin/sin dot) was checked against the Strong's headword for its lemma number. Example roots: 3rd radical א; 1st radical not guttural/נ/י/ו; 2nd radical not guttural/ר/ו/י; not geminate (so בוא, יצא, נשׂא, קרא, ירא, חטא are never examples). Ketiv excluded. Imperatives may carry paragogic ה; infinitives construct may carry a preposition (examplePrefix). Example preference: teaching root, then another root of the class; each in order no prefix, ו, preposition. Every matched token was cross-checked against STEPBible TAHOT; tokens where TAHOT disagrees are never used as examples.

notes.quiescentAleph: The א is kept in writing exactly as WLC writes it. Where it quiesces it has no vowel or shewa of its own (מָצָא, מָצָאתָ, תִּמְצֶאנָה); before a vowel it is a consonant (מָצְאָה, יִמְצְאוּ) (GKC §74.1-3). WLC occasionally omits a quiescent א (מָצָתִי Nu 11:11; GKC §74 Rem. 4); such spellings are not used as examples.
notes.noDageshLene: Because the א quiesces, the following ת/נ afformative is not after a closed syllable and has no dagesh lene: מָצָאתָ, not מָצָאתָּ (GKC §74.2).
notes.cohortative: Cohortative = 1st-person yiqtol + ָה: אֶמְצְאָה. Shown as a note, not a table row.
notes.jussive: As in the strong verb, the jussive looks like yiqtol except in Hiphil (יַמְצֵא vs יַמְצִיא).
notes.weqatal: וּמָצָאתָ (Davidson p. 176). Shown as a note, not a column.
notes.qalStativeType: Stative III-Aleph verbs (מָלֵא, יָרֵא, טָמֵא, צָמֵא) keep ṣere in all persons of the perfect: מָלֵאתִי (GKC §74 Rem. 1; Paradigm O second Qal column; Davidson p. 176 מָלֵא column). Note only, not cells (ruling).
notes.lhConfusion: Some III-Aleph forms follow III-He patterns and vice versa (GKC §75 nn-rr). Such forms are not used as examples.
notes.Hophal imperative: None: GKC Paradigm O and Davidson p. 177 mark it 'wanting'.
